messages.author: 020cb925f39fe64e
messages.subject: ARGOS error ellipses missing
parts:
Hi Chris,

I am very new to movement ecology and I'm trying to analyze the breeding home range of songbirds with Argos data. I uploaded my original Argos DIAG file to Movebank and then imported it from Movebank to R. When using as.telemetry(), it says "(all) ARGOS error ellipses missing. Using location class estimates from Vincent et al (2002)". Do you know if this is the normal case with Argos data or did I do something wrong in the process? I also downloaded the csv file from Argos and it has all error radius, Semi-major axis, Semi-minor axis, and Ellipse orientation columns there. But the data downloaded from Movebank has blank columns. Maybe I should try uploading the csv instead of the DIAG file to Movebank? Is this something I should be worried about, or is it okay to just proceed with the Vincent et al(2002) estimations? Thank you so much for your help!

Best regards,
Violet

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: ARGOS error ellipses missing
parts:
Hi Violet,

Please try importing a CSV with the ellipse columns for better error ellipses information. Argos errors haven a "X" shaped distribution from the polar orbits and the old location classes do not capture this, while the new error ellipses do.
Movebank should have attributes for the Argos error ellipses.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: ARGOS error ellipses missing
parts:
Hi Violet,
  1. The empirical variograms themselves all look okay to me, though I can't see them contrasted to the fitted models. For amounts of data this small, you can also try CI="Gauss" and/or fast=FALSE in the variograms to improve their CIs and/or irregular time-lag dependence.
  2. The tail end of the variograms don't really matter. There's only one data point (time lag) in that estimate.
  3. You say that some home-range estimates come out very large. I can see that you've turned on the error model, but I can't see the fitted variograms. Did you check for outliers?
Best,
Chris

Hi Chris,

I added the variograms with the fitted model in the new pdf here. Each one is with CI="Gauss",fast=FALSE. I'm leaning toward applying the second one (Including only location class 3 and 2 points) in my following analysis since the home range confidence interval is the smallest, do you think it's a reasonable choice? 

For outliers, yes I checked this time, and I only excluded a few unreasonable ones in the fourth approach. Because I'm studying birds, all the speed results coming from outlie(data) are possible for the species (the highest was around 50cm/s). So I think I'll go discuss with my committee about a maximum distance they can travel for outlier exclusion. 

I have another question about the variograms. I recalled you said in the Animove Lecture that we can see the asymptote as a rough estimation of the animal's home range, however, in my results, the home range estimation from akde is not at all visually close to the asymptote on the variogram. Is this because my Argos data have big errors or I'm not understanding it correctly? Sorry for a bunch of questions at the same time, and thank you so much!!!

Best regards,
Violet

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: ARGOS error ellipses missing
parts:
Hi Violet,

Your attached plots all look pretty good to me. The CIs are all highly overlapping.
For the last plots, where the model's variogram is close to the lower end of the data's variance - the other thing I would check with birds is if you were able to segment out the nesting periods from the data.

The variogram also includes location error and would be asymptote to the sum of home-range size and location-error size in your case.

Best,
Chris
